crater.definition: A bowl-shaped geological formation at the top of a volcano.

lava.definition: Rock that in its molten form (as magma) issues from volcanoes.

magma.definition: Molten rock in the earth's crust.

vent.definition: A hole for the escape of gas or air.

caldera.definition: A large crater caused by the violent explosion of a volcano that collapses into a depression.

cone.definition: The roughly cone-shaped hill built around a volcano's opening.

lava-tube.definition: A tunnel-like passage formed when the surface of a lava flow cools and hardens while molten lava continues moving beneath it.
lava-tube.exampleUsage: Researchers mapped a lava tube from outside its unstable sections.

hot-spring.definition: A natural spring whose water is much warmer than the local yearly air temperature because heat from Earth’s crust warms it.

geyser.definition: A spring that discharges hot water and steam.

fumarole.definition: An opening in or near a volcano that releases steam and volcanic gases.
fumarole.exampleUsage: Scientists monitor gases rising from the fumarole.

eruption.definition: The sudden occurrence of a violent discharge of steam and volcanic material.

lava-flow.definition: The movement of molten rock from an opening or crack in a volcano over a period during an eruption.

ash-cloud.definition: A cloud of fine rock, mineral, and volcanic glass particles thrown into the atmosphere by an eruption.
ash-cloud.exampleUsage: The ash cloud drifted away from the volcano.

pyroclastic-flow.definition: A fast-moving, extremely hot mixture of volcanic gas, ash, and rock that travels down the sides of a volcano.
pyroclastic-flow.exampleUsage: Authorities keep people away from areas threatened by pyroclastic flows.

tremor.definition: A small shaking movement of the ground.

earthquake.definition: Shaking and vibration at the surface of the earth resulting from underground movement along a fault plane or from volcanic activity.

explosion.definition: The act of exploding or bursting.

steam-vent.definition: An opening in rock or soil allows steam and gases from heated underground areas to escape.

mudflow.definition: A fast-moving flow of water mixed with mud, rock, and debris; around volcanoes, a volcanic mudflow is often called a lahar.
mudflow.exampleUsage: The hazard map marks valleys that could carry a mudflow.

gas-emission.definition: The release of a gas from a source into the surrounding atmosphere.

basalt.definition: The commonest type of solidified lava.

obsidian.definition: Acid or granitic glass formed by the rapid cooling of lava without crystallization.

pumice.definition: A light glass formed on the surface of some lavas.

granite.definition: Plutonic igneous rock having visibly crystalline texture.

limestone.definition: A sedimentary rock consisting mainly of calcium that was deposited by the remains of marine animals.
limestone.exampleUsage: The limestone was identified during the lesson.

tuff.definition: Hard volcanic rock composed of compacted volcanic ash.

lava-rock.definition: Rock formed when molten lava cools and becomes solid.
lava-rock.exampleUsage: The field contained dark pieces of lava rock.

volcanic-glass.definition: A natural form of glass created when molten lava cools too quickly for crystals to form.

mineral-crystal.definition: A naturally formed solid mineral with an ordered internal structure and a recognizable crystal shape or pattern.
mineral-crystal.exampleUsage: A mineral crystal was visible in the rock sample.

seismograph.definition: A measuring instrument for detecting and measuring the intensity and direction and duration of movements of the ground (as an earthquake).
seismograph.exampleUsage: The seismograph was used during the activity.

tiltmeter.definition: An instrument that measures very small changes in the slope or tilt of the ground.
tiltmeter.exampleUsage: Scientists use a tiltmeter to monitor changes in the volcano's shape.

gas-analyzer.definition: An instrument that measures the types or concentrations of gases in a sample.
gas-analyzer.exampleUsage: The research team used a gas analyzer from a safe monitoring location.

thermal-camera.definition: A camera that detects infrared radiation and displays differences in surface temperature.
thermal-camera.exampleUsage: The thermal camera showed hotter areas on the volcano.

gps-station.definition: A fixed monitoring site that uses satellite positioning to measure changes in ground position over time.
gps-station.exampleUsage: The GPS station recorded slow ground movement.

weather-station.definition: A site in a network of stations that measures and records meteorological conditions.

drone.definition: Stingless male bee in a colony of social bees (especially honeybees) whose sole function is to mate with the queen.

satellite-image.definition: An image of Earth or another body collected by instruments on an orbiting satellite.
satellite-image.exampleUsage: The satellite image showed the ash plume from above.

sample-kit.definition: A set of labeled containers and tools prepared for collecting scientific samples under approved procedures.
sample-kit.exampleUsage: The research team carried a sealed sample kit.

radiation-detector.definition: An instrument designed to detect or measure ionizing radiation.
radiation-detector.exampleUsage: The radiation detector was part of the scientific monitoring equipment.

lava-field.definition: A broad area of ground covered by solidified lava from past flows.
lava-field.exampleUsage: The old lava field stretched across the valley.

volcanic-island.definition: Describes an island built by volcanic eruptions, as well as features or processes connected with that island.

mountain-peak.definition: The highest point or summit of a mountain.
mountain-peak.exampleUsage: Snow remained near the mountain peak.

valley.definition: Low land between hills or mountains.

cliff.definition: A steep wall of rock or earth.

cave.definition: A geological formation consisting of an underground enclosure with access from the surface of the ground or from the sea.

lake.definition: A large area of water surrounded by land.

steam-cloud.definition: A visible cloud formed when water vapor condenses into tiny droplets.
steam-cloud.exampleUsage: A steam cloud rose where hot ground heated water.

black-sand-beach.definition: A beach covered mainly with dark sand, often formed from volcanic rock fragments.
black-sand-beach.exampleUsage: The island has a black-sand beach formed from volcanic material.

rock-formation.definition: The natural creation of rock inside Earth’s crust occurs when melted material cools, sediments harden, or existing rock changes under heat and pressure.

evacuation-route.definition: A planned path used to move people away from a dangerous area during an emergency.
evacuation-route.exampleUsage: The emergency map clearly marks the evacuation route.

warning-siren.definition: A device that produces a loud siren to alert people that a hazard is present.
warning-siren.exampleUsage: The warning siren was used during the activity.

gas-mask.definition: Protective respiratory equipment designed to filter certain harmful gases, vapors, or particles when fitted and used for its approved purpose.
gas-mask.exampleUsage: Specialist teams use approved respiratory protection in hazardous environments.

hard-hat.definition: A hard hat worn to protect the head at a work site.

protective-suit.definition: Special clothing designed to reduce exposure to specified hazards such as chemicals, heat, or contaminated material.
protective-suit.exampleUsage: The trained response team wore protective suits appropriate to the hazard.

emergency-shelter.definition: A place designated to provide temporary protection, accommodation, or assistance during an emergency.
emergency-shelter.exampleUsage: Residents were directed to an emergency shelter outside the hazard zone.

helicopter.definition: An aircraft without wings that obtains its lift from the rotation of overhead blades.

rescue-team.definition: A trained group organized to help people in dangerous or emergency situations.
rescue-team.exampleUsage: The rescue team waited in a safe staging area.

barrier.definition: Any condition that makes it difficult to make progress or to achieve an objective.

hazard-zone.definition: An area identified as having a significant risk from a dangerous event or condition.
hazard-zone.exampleUsage: Only authorized personnel entered the marked hazard zone.

mantle.definition: The cloak as a symbol of authority.

sulfur.definition: An abundant tasteless odorless multivalent nonmetallic element.

quartz.definition: A hard glossy mineral consisting of silicon dioxide in crystal form.

feldspar.definition: Any of a group of hard crystalline minerals that consist of aluminum silicates of potassium or sodium or calcium or barium.

crystal.definition: A rock formed by the solidification of a substance.

tectonic-plate.definition: A large rigid piece of Earth's outer shell that moves slowly over the underlying mantle.
tectonic-plate.exampleUsage: Many volcanoes occur near the boundaries of tectonic plates.

thermal-vent.definition: An opening where heated water, steam, or gases escape from the ground.
thermal-vent.exampleUsage: Steam rose from a thermal vent near the volcanic area.

dormant.definition: (of e.g. volcanoes) not erupting and not extinct.
